en: Then, for the sake of purifying all time-periods, one should first draw the principal maṇḍala called Anantavijaya, which bestows the fruit of the abode of Śiva. || 1 ||
By the mere sight of him, even those who are great sinners become stainless; having attained the state of Rudra, they rejoice without fear. || 2 ||
The lords of the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
and uragas stand outside the sacrificial ground and behold Anantavijaya.
One of the materials such as hemp and so forth should be long, more than double the length of the mandala;
therein, the thread is said to be triple-stranded, even, and free from knots and the like.
And when the directions have been indicated by fish entering and emerging from the shadows,
those of suspicious mind will attempt to deposit their deposits using a measuring-stake.
The stakes should be made of śiṃśapā, khadira, or the heartwood of the plakṣa tree;
they should be square at their base and rounded at the top of the branches.
Then, one should slowly stretch the cord from the eastern and western stakes to those in the south and north, and likewise from the northeast stake to the southwest stake.
Then the preceptor, having established the fire, the water,
and the peg, should draw a lotus in the center, situated within a pedestal measuring two cubits.
In the front portion measuring six finger-breadths, one should draw the pericarp in the first;
the filaments in the second; and the junctions of the petals in the others.
But in the fourth [section], having likewise fashioned the tips of the petals as a lotus,
one should draw a pathway measuring two cubits situated all around the pedestal.
Outside, the enclosure of deities should be constructed separately using half of the path,
arranged into eight divisions corresponding to the eight openings at the front of the path.
Having first laid out the lines for the outer gate, which is completed at half the width of the street-front,
one should then cast down the colored powders.
Those [colours], well-known and possessing their respective qualities, one should apply along the path of the thread, starting with white and so forth in due order. || 13 ||
It is fashioned with white lines, surrounded on the outside by red and other colors,
endowed with eight straight paths, and is the auspicious Anantavijaya.
The canopy and other decorations of the Supreme Lord should be made with a measurement of one, one and a half, two, or double the stated measure, and should be beautifully adorned. || 15 ||
In its center, one should place the deity, the supreme Śiva, upon the pericarp;
having assigned Īśāna to the head, one should assign the face to the eastern petal.
Likewise, Aghora is in the south, Vāmadeva in the north,
and Sadyojāta in the western petal, again according to the sequence of the array of words.
One should begin with the limbs and so forth in the intermediate directions by this very [method].
One should place the Praṇava at the heart at the base of the southeast corner. 18.
One should place the head in the northeast and the crest-lock in the southwest;
likewise, the armor in the northwest and the weapon at the tip of the southeast, as well as in the north.

One should place the *sarvātmāna* mantra on the head; then the eight-syllable *jvālinī*, which is tawny (*piṅgalā*), on the eastern petal-tip; and one should assign the *netra* mantra on the south-eastern [petal] and the *astra* mantra on the southern [petal]. (20)
Having established the Gāyatrī in the west, one should place the limbs of the Vidyā as before;
then, one should install the Pāśupata mantra within all the petals.
Then one should install Ananta on the eastern seat and Sūkṣma on the southern;
and with invocations, water for honor (arghya), and water for the feet (pādya), one should place Śivottama on the western seat.
Then, having placed and worshipped Ekanetra in the north,
the wise one, being composed, should install Ekarudra in the northeast.
One should worship Trimūrti at the mouth of the sacrifice (the east), then Śrīkaṇṭha in the southwest,
and Śikhaṇḍin in the northwest, on the pedestal in due order.
Then there is the power of the Lord of Knowledge (Vidyeśvarī), renowned as the Root-Vidyā;
she is the primordial form of Śiva, who is to be worshipped in the ritual of sacrifice.
One should worship the two groups on the right and left sides of Ananta, and then worship Sūkṣma and the others belonging to the Goddess in their proper order.
Having thus worshipped the deities of the eight groups situated in the four directions, one should worship the Weapon (astra) stationed in the eight door-locations.
Then, having performed the subsequent rite for the disciple as prescribed, the preceptor, having bowed to the Lord of Gods, should address this petition to Śiva: || 28 ||
Be gracious to me, O Lord of Gods, for I am obedient to your command;
by your grace, let this twice-born man, who enjoys worldly pleasures, attain the supreme abode.
Thus, when his desired fruit has been granted,
he should resort to the root of the path— the source of excellence and liberation.
The practitioner, having worshipped that which is based on the root syllable of the one he wishes to lead away as he desires, should join him to that [state] with the Vāmadeva mantra. || 31 ||
There, having performed the manifestation through the Gāyatrī and the birth through the Sadyojāta mantra,
one should then perform the purification of the office through the Ghora mantra.
Having likewise duly brought about enjoyment (bhoga) for the person here, the preceptor should effect dissolution (laya) through Īśāna during the purification of the path (adhvaśuddhi). || 33 ||
Having severed that noose with the Aghora-weapon mantra, one should cast it away with one's whole being;
then, one should offer six initial oblations with the Śiva-mantra, both separately and collectively.
One should offer these nine and six oblations, as prescribed, in due order to all the stations beginning with Kālāgni and ending with Śiva.
For the sake of purifying the other paths, one should commence the fivefold oblation with each respective mantra, according to the number of words established therein.
The common rule should be known to apply to both the path of worlds (bhuvanādhvan) and the path of levels (padādhvan).
O Brahmins, in the level of Sadāśiva, the form [of the path] is twofold in the world.
The fire-oblation for the paths of the principles (tattva) and phonemes (varṇa) is twice as much as previously stated;
on the cloth (paṭa), in the principle Sadāśiva, and on the path of principles, it is fourfold.
That same [number] becomes tenfold in the path of mantra (mantrādhvan) regarding the syllables and so forth;
and the oblation (homa) which is performed in the path of mantra is doubled in the path of the manifest (sakalādhvan).
By this sequential method, the equality of the two oblations for each pair of paths is to be understood, except for the oblation of the yoga of Śiva. 40.
The fire-oblation (homa) based on the Śiva-yoga is common to the Imperishable (Akṣara);
thereafter, one performs the fivefold oblation and at the conclusion of the oblation, the oblations to the Akṣara. || 41 ||
There shall be one thousand three hundred and four oblations;
this is the number of offerings in the Bhauvana initiation rite.

Likewise, in the ritual procedure for initiation (dīkṣā), the number [of mantras] is stated everywhere exactly and in due order, even without the ritual procedures for the other paths (adhvan). || 43 ||
In the path of the principles (tattvādhvan), one should know that there are fifty-eight thousand oblations;
likewise in the ritual of the path of the phonemes (varṇādhvakarman). || 44 ||
Two thousand two hundred and eight [mantras] are prescribed by the rules of the path of Mantra;
that same number was previously declared as the "Kalā" in the initiation on the Path.
Thus, he who has been initiated by the initiation according to the ritual of the six paths in the Anantavijaya [tantra] is now severed from the bondage consisting of phenomenal existence.
